summary: Well-executed, carefully archived preregistered paired experiment comparing an LLM-only baseline vs a verifier-augmented (guarded) pipeline on 200 synthetic NetOps intent→configuration tasks. Execution and artifact provenance are excellent. However the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics produced identical generated candidates for both arms, producing a ceiling effect (0 unsafe proposals in both arms) that makes the confirmatory McNemar test non-informative for the stated causal question. The manuscript documents this outcome and archives artifacts, but requires targeted manuscript clarifications and rephrasing to avoid overstating the experimental conclusion and to explain the statistical and preregistration consequences of the design choice.
critical_issues: Primary confirmatory hypothesis (H1) about verifier-mediated reduction of unsafe proposals is not testable in the observed data because the preregistered shared_initial_generation design produced identical generated candidates for baseline and guarded arms and yielded zero discordant pairs (n10=n01=0). This ceiling effect invalidates the intended causal contrast and the power assumptions underlying the preregistration; the manuscript must state this limitation unambiguously and revise any language that implies the guarded pipeline ‘failed to reduce’ unsafe proposals in a general sense.

Statistical interpretation: reporting an exact McNemar p=1.0 and a 95% CI [0.0,0.0] without an explicit statement that zero discordant pairs render the paired test non-informative risks misleading readers. The manuscript must add an explicit statistical caveat and explain consequences for the preregistered power calculation and inferential claims.

Manuscript presentation currently mixes extensive provenance/artifact inventory into the main narrative. The CNSM conference paper should prioritize literature-grounded scholarly prose (motivation, method, quantitative result, interpretation, limitations). Move detailed manifest/hashes and exhaustive artifact listings out of the main narrative (refer to the archived execution_manifest) and compress provenance text to satisfy normal conference-style exposition while preserving traceability.
required_revisions: Revise abstract, introduction, results, and conclusion wording to (a) avoid any phrasing that could be read as a general empirical claim that the guarded pipeline 'did not reduce unsafe proposals', and (b) clearly state that under the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics the two arms received the same initial candidate and therefore the confirmatory paired test could not detect verifier-mediated corrections when the shared candidate was already valid. Cite the relevant archived artifacts (execution_manifest) for reproducibility.

Add an explicit statistical clarification in Methods and Results: explain that McNemar/exact paired tests require discordant pairs to detect differences; report that n10=n01=0 therefore the test is non-informative for causal effect detection here, and that the preregistered power assumptions were violated (baseline unsafe rate ≠ assumed). Discuss how this changes interpretation of the pre-specified hypothesis and conclusions.

Compress provenance and artifact inventory in the body: move full hash lists, per-task file listings, and exhaustive manifest entries to a clearly referenced archival appendix or supplemental artifact bundle (execution_manifest path). Replace body-level provenance with concise references to the archived manifest and a short machine-readable provenance pointer. Ensure the main text reads as normal scholarly prose with focused methodological description, quantitative results, interpretation, and limitations.

Clarify terminology and labels: define 'success' vs 'unsafe proposal' consistently (e.g., success = no verifier-detected violation) and ensure all tables/figures/captions and the abstract use that terminology consistently to avoid confusion (the current files label counts as 'success' which can confuse readers).
optional_revisions: Add a brief, explicit evidence-to-claim table (1 paragraph or a single compact table) in the manuscript summarizing which claims are supported directly by confirmatory analysis, which are exploratory, and which are limitations/inferences—referencing archived artifact paths for each item.

Add a short discussion item recommending alternative preregistered generation semantics (independent per-condition generation) and sample-size/attack-strength prescriptions for a repeat confirmatory test; illustrate using numbers from the preregistration’s power calculation to help future replication (no new experiments required).

If space permits, shorten or move one representative provenance example (e.g., one task’s baseline vs guarded scoring JSON) to the supplement and include a single concise in-text illustrative example showing how a verifier trace looks and why identical candidates arose.
